mainEntity.name: How much does a Kia e-Niro drive unit replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Kia e-Niro drive unit typically costs £1,800-£3,400 supply-only, depending on the unit (EM57 or PE95) and condition. Used units start from £800. Supply & fit adds £450-£850 labour, with EV-certified technicians required for installation.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing Kia e-Niro drive unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of a failing Kia e-Niro drive unit include a whining, milling or tapping noise that increases with speed, a grinding noise from the front of the vehicle, loss of drive power, and a 'Refill Inverter Coolant' warning on the dashboard.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the drive unit in a Kia e-Niro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Kia e-Niro drive unit is usually worthwhile if the battery, body and interior are in good condition. A reconditioned drive unit costs £1,800-£3,800 versus £8,000-£25,000 for a comparable used e-Niro. The battery is the most valuable component - if it is healthy, drive unit replacement is almost always justified.

mainEntity.name: How long do Kia e-Niro drive units last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, Kia e-Niro drive units regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. However, some early-production units have experienced reduction gearbox bearing wear from 50,000km (31,000 miles) onwards. Regular gearbox oil changes and avoiding prolonged high-speed driving can extend lifespan significantly.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the EM57 and PE95 drive units?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EM57 is fitted to first-generation e-Niros (2019-2022) and produces 150kW (201hp) with 395 Nm of torque in the 64kWh version, or 100kW (134hp) in the 39kWh version. The PE95 is fitted to second-generation e-Niros (2022-present) and produces 150kW (201hp) with 255 Nm of torque. Both are permanent-magnet synchronous motors.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Kia e-Niro drive unit code before ordering a replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Kia e-Niro drive unit code appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the drive unit casing, or on your V5C registration document. Common codes include EM57 (2019-2022, all battery sizes) and PE95 (2022-present, 64.8kWh). Enter your reg above for instant verification and compatible quotes.

historyTimeline.h2: Kia e-Niro - Electric Drive Unit History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Kia e-Niro (also known as the Niro EV) launched in 2019 as Kia's first dedicated electric crossover in the UK, combining the popular Niro body style with a zero-emission powertrain. Unlike the hybrid Niro models which use the G4LE combustion engine, the e-Niro is powered exclusively by a permanent-magnet synchronous electric motor paired with a single-speed reduction gearbox - making it a pure EV with no internal combustion engine.

milestones.description: **2019** - e-Niro launched with 64kWh battery and 150kW (201hp) EM57 electric motor
**2020** - Entry-level 39kWh battery introduced with 100kW (134hp) motor, still EM57 code
**2021** - Minor software updates to battery management and thermal systems
**2022** - Second-generation (SG2) e-Niro arrives with PE95 drive unit, 150kW motor and 64.8kWh battery

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every EM57 and PE95 drive unit fitted to the Kia e-Niro is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Kia e-Niro Electric Drive Unit Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Kia e-Niro's electric drive unit is generally reliable, but a small number of high-mileage and early-production examples have experienced reduction gearbox bearing wear, GDU bolt issues and inverter coolant pump failures. These problems dominate UK replacement enquiries for the e-Niro, particularly on examples approaching 50,000-100,000 miles. Every reconditioned drive unit through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Reduction Gearbox Bearing Wear - Why Kia e-Niro Drive Units Develop Whining Noises
problems.rootCause: The reduction gearbox uses ball bearings that can wear prematurely, particularly on vehicles used for high-speed motorway driving or those that have never had the gearbox oil changed. This presents as a whining, milling or tapping noise that increases with speed. The issue is well-documented in owner forums, with some reporting the problem as early as 13,000 miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of motor and reduction gearbox bearings using a third-party repair kit
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; restores normal operation without full unit replacement

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete removal and replacement of the drive unit with a reconditioned EM57 or PE95 unit, including full system calibration
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix; includes 12-month warranty and addresses all potential failure points

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Kia e-Niro is worth roughly **£8,000-£25,000** depending on age, mileage, battery size and condition. A reconditioned drive unit at specialist pricing (£1,800-£3,400 supply & fit) represents **10-30% of the vehicle's value** - comfortably justified for most examples. For higher-mileage 2019 examples approaching £8,000, a used drive unit may be a more economical alternative.
problems.recommendation: If your Kia e-Niro develops a whining or milling noise, have it diagnosed by an EV specialist immediately. The third-party bearing repair kit can be a cost-effective solution if caught early. However, if the noise is severe or accompanied by grinding, the damage may have extended to the GDU housing - in which case a full reconditioned drive unit is the only reliable fix. Anecdotal reports suggest dealers may replace components piecemeal in an attempt to run out the warranty; our specialists provide a single, transparent solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare reconditioned EM57 Kia e-Niro drive unit prices

problems.h4: Gear Drive Unit (GDU) Bolt Failure - Why Kia e-Niro Drive Units Can Lose Power
problems.rootCause: The differential gear bolts within the GDU may not have been tightened to the correct torque during assembly. Over time, these bolts can loosen and damage the GDU housing and/or reduction gear while driving. Continued driving with a grinding noise may result in a loss of drive power and/or cause the differential to lock up. Kia issued a recall for certain 2023MY Niro EV vehicles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete GDU assembly replacement at no cost to the customer
repairOptions.longevity: If your vehicle is affected by the recall, this is the only option - and it's free

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete removal and replacement of the drive unit with a reconditioned PE95 unit, including full system calibration
repairOptions.longevity: If the recall does not apply or the vehicle is out of warranty, a reconditioned unit is the safest option

problems.recommendation: Check if your Kia e-Niro is affected by the GDU bolt recall. Kia dealers will replace the GDU assembly free of charge. If your vehicle is not covered or you are experiencing symptoms outside the recall period, a full reconditioned PE95 unit with verified torque specifications is the safest long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Check if your Kia e-Niro is affected by the GDU recall

problems.h4: Inverter Coolant Pump Failure - Why Kia e-Niros Display "Refill Inverter Coolant" Warnings
problems.rootCause: The original inverter coolant (BSC-1) can crystallise over time, damaging the electric water pump and causing coolant flow issues. This triggers a "Refill Inverter Coolant" warning on the dashboard, even when coolant levels appear normal. A TSB was issued for 2018-2019MY Niro EV vehicles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Flush of inverter cooling system, replacement of coolant with new formula (BSC-2), replacement of electric water pump if faulty
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective; addresses the root cause of the warning
Only necessary if coolant pump failure has led to inverter or motor damage

problems.recommendation: The "Refill Inverter Coolant" warning is a known issue on early e-Niros. A coolant flush and pump replacement is a relatively inexpensive fix that should be addressed promptly to prevent damage to the inverter. Do not ignore this warning - continued driving with insufficient coolant flow can damage the drive unit.
